unit-m3u8.title: Unit 3 · Lesson 8: Bar Diagrams for Multiplication
unit-m3u8.source: enVision Topic 3 textbook scan — Multiply Multi-Digit Whole Numbers (Drive)

summary.text: Lesson 3-8 of the Topic 3 textbook scan: using bar diagrams and variables to write and solve multiplication equations for "times as many" problems.

why.text: A bar diagram makes "times as many" visible, which is what stops her from adding when she should be multiplying.

objectives.text: Draw a bar diagram for a "times as many" problem
Write and solve an equation with a variable

parentNote.text: The mistake these questions keep offering is adding the "times" number instead of multiplying ($1,340 + 5). The other is drawing the bars backwards — giving the longer bar to the person with less. One lv3 question is built entirely around which bar is which, since that is where the rest of the problem goes right or wrong.

nextUp.text: Draw it, write the equation, multiply.

cards.def:
**If one amount is 5 times as many as another, multiply the smaller amount by 5.**
• 5 times as much as $1,340 is $1,340 × 5.
cards.hint: "Times as many" is a multiplication signal.

cards.def:
**Draw one bar for the smaller amount and a longer bar made of equal copies of it.**
• 5 times as many → the long bar has 5 equal sections.
cards.hint: Count the sections — that is the number you multiply by.

cards.def:
**A letter stands for the number you are trying to find.**
• Let p = the new price. Then p = 1,340 × 5.
cards.hint: The letter is a placeholder for the answer.

cards.def:
**Turn the bar diagram into an equation, then solve it.**
• 1,340 × 5 = p, so p = 6,700.

**Use estimation or repeated addition to check.**
• 1,340 × 5 is about 1,300 × 5 = 6,500 — close to 6,700.
cards.hint: A quick estimate catches big mistakes.

questions.q: A painting sold for $1,340. Years later it sold for 5 times as much. Which equation finds the new price, p?
questions.hint: "5 times as much" is a multiplication.
steps: The new price is 5 times the old price.

ex.tip: Adding 5 would make it only $5 more — nowhere near 5 times.

questions.q: A painting sold for $1,340. Years later it sold for 5 times as much. What was the later price?
Sharon's store has 2,415 stickers. May's store has 4 times as many. How many stickers does May's store have?
questions.hint: Draw a bar with 4 equal sections of 2,415.

questions.q: There are 16 buses. Each bus has 48 seats. How many seats are there in all?
questions.hint: The bar diagram has 16 equal sections of 48.

ex.tip: 64 is 16 + 48. Sixteen equal groups means multiply.

questions.q: Priya lives 14 times as far from the beach as Leo. Leo lives 36 miles away. How far away does Priya live?

ex.tip: 144 is only 36 × 4 — the tens row got left out.

questions.q: A pond holds 1,250 gallons. A pool holds 12 times as much. How many gallons does the pool hold?

ex.tip: 12,500 is only 1,250 × 10 — the ones row is missing.

questions.q: Ana read 3 times as many pages as Ben. Ben read 214 pages. Which bar diagram shows this?
opts: Ana's bar is 214 sections, each 3 pages long
Ana's bar is 1 section of 214; Ben's bar is 3 sections of 214
Ana's bar is 3 sections, each 214; Ben's bar is 1 section of 214
Both bars are 3 sections, because the story says 3
questions.hint: Who read MORE? Their bar is longer.
steps: Ana read 3 times as many, so she read more.
Her bar is 3 copies of Ben's bar.
Ben's bar is one section of 214.

ex.main: **Ana's bar is 3 sections of 214; Ben's is 1.** Ana read 642 pages.
ex.tip: Getting the bars backwards gives the right numbers to the wrong people.

questions.q: One factory makes 265 bikes a day. Another makes 13 times as many. How many bikes does the second factory make each day?

ex.tip: 1,060 adds 265 × 3 and 265 × 1 — the 1 in 13 means 1 ten.

questions.q: How can estimation show that $1,340 × 5 = $6,700 is reasonable?
steps: 6,700 is close to 6,500, so the answer is reasonable.

ex.main: **1,300 × 5 = 6,500, which is close.** The exact answer lands right near the estimate.
ex.tip: An estimate never proves an exact answer — it shows it is the right size.

questions.q: One store has 2,415 stickers and another has 4 times as many. In the equation s = 2,415 × 4, what does the letter s stand for?
opts: The number 4, since it is the number beside the ×
The unknown number of stickers in the second store
The word "stickers" written in a shorter way
Any number at all that you would like to pick
questions.hint: What is the question asking you to find?
steps: A variable stands for an unknown number.
Here it is the number of stickers in the second store.

ex.main: **The unknown number of stickers.** The variable holds the place of the answer.
ex.tip: Choosing a letter that matches the story — s for stickers — makes it easy to remember.
